item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find a single public 2024 document that lays out a comprehensive, line-item presidential plan with budget figures, deadlines, and enforcement milestones across all major sectors. The available evidence is fragmented across official speeches, IMF/World Bank program documents, and rights reporting. That means we can see implementation intent and some concrete mechanisms, but not a fully transparent, integrated execution dashboard.","evidence":[{"title":"President El-Sisi meets prime minister and members of the new government","publisher":"State Information Service","date":"Jul. 3, 2024","url":"https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/president-el-sisi-meets-prime-minister-and-members-of-the-new-government/","summary":"Sisi told the new government to strengthen institutional frameworks, improve coordination across ministries and state agencies, and emphasize integrity and transparency. This is concrete translation of program into governance instructions, and it directly informs how the 2024 cabinet was supposed to function.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.1"]},{"title":"President Sisi swears in new government ministers","publisher":"State Information Service","date":"Jul. 3, 2024","url":"https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/president-sisi-swears-in-new-government-ministers/","summary":"The reshuffle installed technocratic portfolios in economic management, energy, science, foreign affairs, and other policy-heavy areas. That is a concrete personnel move aligned with the stated program.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.1"]},{"title":"IMF staff and authorities reach agreement on reviews under the EFF","publisher":"IMF","date":"Mar. 6, 2024","url":"https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/03/06/pr-2459-egypt-staff-and-authorities-reach-agreement-on-reviews-under-the-eff-arrangement","summary":"The authorities agreed to a flexible exchange rate, tighter fiscal and monetary policy, more social spending for vulnerable groups, and reforms to remove preferential treatment for state-owned enterprises. This is one of the clearest examples of turning program into specific policy priorities with operational content.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.1"]},{"title":"IMF reaches agreement on the 3rd review of the EFF","publisher":"IMF","date":"Jun. 6, 2024","url":"https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/06/06/pr-24208-egypt-imf-reaches-agreement-on-the-3rd-review-of-the-eff","summary":"The reform agenda was tied to private-sector-led growth, fiscal space for health and education, and reducing the state’s role in the economy. This is a concrete policy roadmap rather than general rhetoric.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.1"]},{"title":"IMF executive board completes 3rd review","publisher":"IMF","date":"Jul. 29, 2024","url":"https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/29/pr24293-egypt-imf-exec-board-completes-3rd-rev-extended-arr-eff","summary":"The IMF reported easing inflation, eliminated FX shortages, and protected social spending as part of ongoing stabilization. That indicates the program was being carried through by macro policy instruments and not just announced.","question_ids":["8B.2"]},{"title":"Promoting Inclusive Human Capital Development and Building Resilience in Egypt through Cash Transfer Programs","publisher":"World Bank","date":"May 28, 2024","url":"https://www.worldbank.org/en/results/2024/05/28/promoting-inclusive-human-capital-development-and-building-resilience-in-egypt-through-cash-transfer-programs","summary":"Takaful and Karama is described as institutionalized, well-targeted, and linked to health, education, and women’s empowerment, with a 55 percent benefit increase. This is concrete social-policy implementation with delivery mechanisms.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.1"]},{"title":"Women’s Empowerment Strategy 2030","publisher":"State Information Service","date":"Mar. 12, 2024","url":"https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/strategies/womens-empowerment-strategy-2030/","summary":"The presidency assigned the strategy to government and state agencies, with explicit priorities around equal opportunity, labor participation, legal protection, and social integration. That is a policy framework with institutional assignment, not just a slogan.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.1"]},{"title":"Minister of labor: ministry has a strategy to empower women","publisher":"State Information Service","date":"Mar. 23, 2024","url":"https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/minister-labor-ministry-has-strategy-to-empower-women/","summary":"The ministry said it was creating training programs, job-placement tools, and a gender-equality unit at Sisi’s direction. This is a concrete implementation layer beneath the broader women’s strategy.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.1"]},{"title":"President El-Sisi’s speech at the El-Dabaa nuclear plant foundation ceremony","publisher":"State Information Service","date":"Jan. 23, 2024","url":"https://sis.gov.eg/en/presidency/speeches-telegrams-posts/el-sisi-s-speech-at-the-official-ceremony-of-laying-the-foundation-stone-for-power-unit-4-at-el-dabaa-nuclear-power-plant/","summary":"Sisi tied nuclear power to energy security, long-term supply, reduced fossil dependence, and development. That shows a specific sectoral priority translated into infrastructure program language.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.1"]},{"title":"Egypt tabled a 2024 draft resolution calling for a Middle East nuclear-weapon-free zone","publisher":"UN Digital Library","date":"Oct. 14, 2024","url":"https://digitallibrary.un.org/record/4063948?ln=en","summary":"This shows the state operationalizing its stated nonproliferation posture through a formal diplomatic initiative. It is one of the few clear examples of a program being turned into an institutional action.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.1"]},{"title":"Egypt’s foreign ministry said the state would use its IAEA Board seat to promote nuclear safety/security","publisher":"Egypt Ministry of Foreign Affairs","date":"Sep. 19, 2024","url":"https://www.mfa.gov.eg/ar/MediaMinistries/Details/MinistryNews/185","summary":"The foreign ministry described a specific institutional role for Egypt inside the IAEA, tied to safety/security and a nuclear-weapon-free-zone agenda. That is a concrete institutional channel for implementation.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.1"]},{"title":"The president directs referral of the National Dialogue’s recommendations to the government","publisher":"Presidency of the Republic of Egypt","date":"Aug. 21, 2024","url":"https://www.presidency.eg/en/%D9%82%D8%B3%D9%85_%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1/%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1_%D8%B1%D8%A6%D8%A7%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%A9/news2182024/","summary":"Sisi instructed the government to implement recommendations on shortening pretrial detention, activating alternatives to detention, and compensating wrongful detention. This is a direct example of a program being translated into enforcement and procedural reform instructions.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.1"]},{"title":"Case 173 closure and lifting of some travel bans","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"Jul. 15, 2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/07/15/human-rights-watch-submission-universal-periodic-review-egypt","summary":"HRW said some travel bans were lifted and Case 173 was announced closed, but asset freezes and terrorism charges persisted. That is a limited institutional easing, but it shows partial enforcement change.","question_ids":["8B.2"]},{"title":"Egypt: Civic Space Under Siege","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"Jan. 11, 2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/egypt-civic-space-under-siege","summary":"HRW said authorities curtailed free expression and peaceful assembly to stymie meaningful competition. This shows enforcement mechanisms being used for control rather than for programmatic implementation through open institutions.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.1"]},{"title":"Egypt: Court Punishes Activists Challenging al-Sisi","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"Feb. 8, 2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/02/08/egypt-court-punishes-activists-challenging-al-sisi","summary":"The court sentence and election ban for Tantawy and supporters show the regime using legal institutions to deter opposition. That cuts against any claim that institutions were being strengthened in a neutral way.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.1"]},{"title":"Egypt: Spate of Free Speech Prosecutions","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"Aug. 29, 2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/29/egypt-spate-free-speech-prosecutions","summary":"HRW reported renewed prosecutions of critics and journalists, including cases tied to corruption reporting involving senior pro-Sisi party members. This suggests the implementation system still shielded the ruling network from scrutiny.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.1"]},{"title":"Egypt: Halt crackdown on people voicing concerns over economic crisis","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"May 13, 2024","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/egypt-halt-crackdown-on-people-voicing-concerns-over-economic-crisis/","summary":"Amnesty documented arrests of protesters, striking workers, and online critics over economic discontent. That is enforcement in the opposite direction from a transparent reform program.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.1"]},{"title":"Egypt: More than 100 arbitrarily detained over calls for anti-government protests","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"Jul. 18, 2024","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/egypt-more-than-100-arbitrarily-detained-over-calls-for-anti-government-protests/","summary":"Security forces detained 119 people after online protest calls over prices and power cuts. This shows a coercive enforcement mechanism still dominating in practice.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.1"]},{"title":"Freedom in the World 2024: Egypt","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/egypt/freedom-world/2024","summary":"Freedom House says Sisi and the security apparatus dominate policymaking and the corruption watchdog is controlled by Sisi. That indicates weak separation between program, institutions, and enforcement.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.1"]},{"title":"Freedom on the Net 2024: Egypt","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/egypt/freedom-net/2024","summary":"The state continued blocking sites and allowing censorship without judicial approval, showing information-control enforcement rather than open implementation.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.1"]},{"title":"Human Rights Watch synthesis on Sisi and the military/security services","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"Feb. 26, 2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/02/26/egypts-al-sisi-has-caged-himself","summary":"HRW argues Sisi relies on coercion and the military/security services rather than a normal party structure, and that independent institutions have been hollowed out. This is strong evidence against durable institutional translation of the program.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.1"]},{"title":"U.S. Department of State investment climate report","publisher":"U.S. Department of State","date":"2024","url":"https://2021-2025.state.gov/reports/2024-investment-climate-statements/egypt/","summary":"The report says SOEs and military-owned companies still enjoy significant advantages, including regulatory relief and tax exemptions, while private firms complain about inconsistent enforcement. That shows the program did not fully translate into equal rules in practice.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.1"]},{"title":"OECD Economic Surveys: Egypt 2024","publisher":"OECD","date":"2024","url":"https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/oecd-economic-surveys-egypt-2024_af900de2-en/full-report/component-8.html","summary":"OECD says military-owned firms benefit from tax and land/resource advantages and that ownership structures are opaque. That is direct evidence that formal policy had not yet displaced entrenched privilege.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.1"]}]}
